A few bits I forgot to add earlier:

Gas station attendants will almost always know the surrounding area and are happy to offer directions or recommend their favorite places in the area if you ask nicely. They get asked for directions all the time.

Tipping is something many other countries find strange, and if you eat at restaurants you'll be in that situation very often. It's simple: leave some cash tucked under your plate and the waitress will pick it up as she cleans the table. No tip is a punishment for rude servers, 10% is default, 20% is a sign of good service, anything about 30% is excessive but still appreciated. There will be a "Tip" amount listed on the bill if you pay with a card - tip in cash whenever possible and mark that as ZERO. (Some places will tip themselves if you leave that blank) Be aware when paying with a card that registers will initially charge about double the bill and then return the excess once they know your tip amount - if you have a card with $40 on it, it may be rejected on a $20 restaurant bill!

The only other time tipping is expected is when ordering drinks at a bar, in which case you can expect a direct correlation between their speed of service and how well you've tipped. They'll make full change from cash and give you everything, leaving a few dollars on their side of the bar is code for "theirs."

Biker bars often get depicted very harshly in the movies, but many will be welcoming of a fellow biker. Use your best judgment.
